subject: CatalystHealth — post-demo SLO clarification & hardware path
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>

Subject: CatalystHealth — post-demo notes + clarification on perf targets

Alexis — great demo earlier, appreciate the time. Quick recap and asks so we can size a dedicated pilot: 

Summary from call:
- Goal: put Redwood Dedicated behind a production inference path for interactive clinical summarization (front-door API to EHR ingestion).
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~150 requests/sec (mix of short & long).
- Peak bursts: up to ~400 RPS for short windows (1–5 min).
- Concurrency: client-side parallelism may reach ~50–60 concurrent live sessions.
- Streaming: must support token-stream partials so patients see results progressively; client will assemble.
- Latency target: p95 end-to-end <= 200ms for the common case (requests that generate up to ~600 output tokens).

Asks / data we need to finalize sizing and GPU recommendation:
1) Typical request size (input tokens) and average output tokens for the workflows we saw — please provide distribution if possible (p50/p95).
2) Expected ratio of short (<=128 tokens) vs long (>=512 tokens) responses.
3) Any hard SLOs for cold-start tail (e.g., max time to first token when model/slot warm?)
4) Procurement lead / timing for pilot contract and SOC2 evidence requests.

Attached is an initial SLO matrix (slo-matrix-v1.xlsx) and a short GPU tradeoffs brief we'll fill in after you share the token distribution. My ask: can you reply with the token distribution and confirm procurement contact? We'll then propose a 2-week pilot configuration (hardware options + expected reserved throughput) and a sample mutual action plan.

Next steps I propose:
- You: token distribution + procurement contact (today/tomorrow)
- Us: follow-up with two concrete dedicated pool configs (H100-based and A100-based) + pilot cost estimate (within 48 hours of your distribution)
- Align on pilot week in June (recommended)

Thanks — Rishi

--

Thanks Rishi — good recap. Quick answers inline.

Token distribution (approx, production expectation):
- Input (prompt + context): p50 = 220 tokens, p95 = 410 tokens.
- Output (model-generated): p50 = 420 tokens, p95 = 780 tokens.
- Mix: ~60% short (<=256 outputs), 30% medium (257–600), 10% long (>600).

Concurrency/throughput notes:
- 150 RPS steady is accurate for our pilot traffic morphology; bursts up to 380 RPS expected during morning sync windows.
- Concurrency: peak of ~55 concurrent live sessions observed in existing traffic.
- Streaming required — must send partial tokens as they are generated; client will do final assembly and dedup.

SLOs:
- p95 time-to-first-token (TTFT) must be <= 120ms for short requests; for long responses p95 <= 220ms is acceptable.
- End-to-end p95 (full response) <= 200ms for responses under 512 tokens is a soft target; acceptable degradation for >512 tokens as long as streaming starts quickly.

Procurement: looping in Procurement and Samuel (technical buyer) — procurement@catalysthealth.com is the correct mailbox. They will ask for SOC2, uptime SLA, and data handling docs.

I'll attach a short internal doc with sample payloads in case that helps. Happy to jump on a follow-up call after you send configs.

— Alexis
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Alexis Turner <alexis.turner@catalysthealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 06 Jun 2028 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: CatalystHealth — post-demo notes + clarification on perf targets

Alexis — thanks for the distribution, that's very helpful. A few engineering notes and two concrete hardware/throughput options below. Attaching a short PDF with microbenchmarks (gpu-comparison-brief.pdf).

Quick observations based on your numbers:
- Heavy tail (10% >600 output tokens) means we should optimize for both streaming start (TTFT) and sustained token throughput.
- Batch-friendly short requests will benefit from batching; long streaming requests reduce batching efficiency but we can use dynamic batching + prefix cache.

Option A — H100 (preferred if latency SLOs are strict):
- Model class: fp16/quant-aware run (no lossy quantization for now).
- Suggested pool: 6x H100-80GB in a dedicated pool.
- Reserved throughput estimate: ~160 steady RPS sustained (concurrency headroom to handle 55 concurrent sessions), burst capacity up to ~380 RPS using short-window autoscale.
- Expected p95 TTFT (short requests): ~90–120ms; long responses p95 start ~150–220ms depending on token length.
- Notes: H100 gives better kernel perf and longer sustained throughput under streaming workloads. Pricing higher than A100.

Option B — A100 80GB (cost-optimized):
- Suggested pool: 8x A100-80GB.
- Reserved throughput estimate: ~140 steady RPS with careful batching and aggressive KV caching; peak bursts supported with temporary burst nodes but with slower TTFT during bursts.
- Expected p95 TTFT (short): ~110–180ms; long-response streaming start will be similar but sustained throughput slightly lower than H100.
- Notes: cheaper, good for cost-constrained pilots, but requires more careful request shaping/queueing.

Operational guardrails / suggested pilot config:
- 2-week pilot: dedicated pool + warmup traffic generator (we can replay a 72-hour slice).
- Acceptance criteria: p95 TTFT <= 150ms for >80% of short requests, system keeps within reserved throughput without >5% error rate.
- Telemetry: token-level tracing, prefix cache hit-rate dashboard, slot utilization.

Next step asks from engineering:
- Can you provide a 15–30 minute sample traffic dump (anonymized) or histograms for token lengths and inter-arrival times? That will let us produce a tighter sizing curve and cost estimate.
- Any strict budget cap we should honor for the pilot?

I'll draft a short mutual action plan once we agree on which option you want to pursue.

— Soojin
